name: tabular_survival_cox
title: Time-to-event modelling with lifelines and scikit-survival: a Cox model, a Kaplan-Meier baseline and a random survival forest inside a Pipeline
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the unknown-framework honesty probe

forbidden.why: every fit takes train_frame, which the split at line 55 produced: cox.fit at line 68, kaplan.fit at line 74 and forest.fit at line 115. The imputer and the scaler are Pipeline steps and are never fitted on their own
test_frame reaches predict_partial_hazard at line 95, forest.predict at line 98 and the two concordance calls; nothing is ever fitted on it
the estimator handed to cross_val_score at line 89 is build_forest(), a Pipeline whose first two steps are the imputer and the scaler - which is the fix MLV103 asks for
months_observed is a duration, not a timestamp: nothing parses a date, converts one or sorts by one, so a stratified random split over subjects is the right split for this design
no class metric is called anywhere; concordance_index and concordance_index_censored are rank statistics and are in neither metric list
there is no roc_auc_score or average_precision_score in this project
seed_everything() seeds random and numpy at lines 43-44, the split and the KFold carry random_state=SEED, and the survival forest carries random_state=SEED
train_test_split at line 55 and KFold at line 88 both pass random_state=SEED
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no lifelines or sksurv equivalent
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a lifelines program
no device is ever named in this project
nothing is pickled or loaded here

notes: This project is in the corpus for what MLView SAYS about it, not only for what it finds. Both lifelines and sksurv are unknown to the knowledge tables, and the analyzer emits one unresolved_callee diagnostic per package naming the exact calls it read without understanding (CoxPHFitter, KaplanMeierFitter, concordance_index; RandomSurvivalForest, concordance_index_censored). That declaration is the behaviour under test: a silent zero-finding run on a workspace built on two unknown libraries would be the failure.

The graph score for this program is therefore expected to be low and must not be 'fixed' by hand-drawing fewer ops: seven of the seventeen ops are calls into the two unknown packages, and they are labelled precisely so the cost of not knowing them is measured.

MLV105 (target left inside the feature matrix) is catalogued but NOT implemented, so it cannot carry a forbidden label; recorded here instead because this file is its sharpest trap. fit_cox at line 68 deliberately hands the duration and event columns to the estimator alongside the covariates, because duration_col= and event_col= is the lifelines API. That is the target travelling with the feature frame by design, not a target left in the feature matrix, and a rule that keys on the surface fires here.
